predecessors.name: House of Jagiellon
predecessors.text: the Crown of Poland and the Grand Duchy of Lithuania of the Jagiellonian realm, joined by the Union of Lublin (1 July 1569); the Lithuanian half includes its Ukrainian and Belarusian lands

successors.name: Russian Empire
successors.text: the Third Partition share of 24 October 1795, 'including Vilnius' (120,000 km2); Russia had taken the lands east of the Dvina-Dnieper line in 1772 and central Belarus and Ukraine in 1793

successors.name: Habsburg monarchy
successors.text: the Third Partition share 'including Lublin and Kraków' (47,000 km2); Galicia had gone to Austria in 1772

successors.name: Kingdom of Prussia
successors.text: the Third Partition share 'including Warsaw' (48,000-55,000 km2); Prussia had taken Royal Prussia in 1772 and Greater Poland in 1793

rulers.name: Sigismund II Augustus
rulers.title: King of Poland and Grand Duke of Lithuania

rulers.name: Henry III of France (Henry of Valois)

ledger.x: 1569: the Union of Lublin creates the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, with Kraków as capital.
1569: the Jagiellonian realm (house-of-jagiellon, the Crown and the Grand Duchy of Lithuania) is merged into the Commonwealth; the Grand Duchy enters as its second constituent.
1569: Courland is a vassal of the Commonwealth.

19 July 1569, Lublin: 'Duke Albert Frederick rendered King Sigismund II homage and was in return installed as Duke of Prussia'; the duke was 'formally a vassal of the crown of Poland' (the fief dates from the Prussian Homage of 10 April 1525).

1569: 'After the Union of Lublin in 1569, it became a joint domain of the Polish Crown and the Grand Duchy'; 'It was a province of Grand Duchy of Lithuania until 1569' and 'a semi-autonomous vassal state of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania'.
1579: Báthory's campaign opens with Polotsk.
30 August 1579: Báthory retakes Polotsk.
1582: the Truce of Jam Zapolski, in which 'Russia would surrender all areas in Livonia it still held' and 'Polotsk would remain under Commonwealth control'.
1582: the Truce of Jam Zapolski ends the fighting with Russia over Livonia.
1585: 'Sevsk' is listed as gained by Feodor I of Russia from the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth.
1595: the Cossack rising takes towns.
1596: the capital moves from Kraków to Warsaw.
July 1596: the rising is crushed.
1609: the Polish siege of Smolensk begins.
1610: Polish troops occupy Moscow.

2 June 1611: 'On 2 June 1611 Smolensk had finally fallen to the Poles' (Polish–Russian War (1609–1618) page; the same page also gives 13 June 1611 for the mine attack, 'The fortress fell on the same day': both June).
1611: the 1609-1611 siege is over (see the gain).
4 November 1612: 'Commonwealth forces were eventually driven out' of Moscow.
'The duchy was inherited by the Hohenzollern prince-electors of Brandenburg in 1618.

1618: the Elector of Brandenburg holds Ducal Prussia as the same Polish fief until the Treaties of Wehlau (19 September 1657) and Bromberg (6 November 1657). brandenburg-prussia has no vassal events of its own for this.
4 January 1619: the Truce of Deulino hands over Chernihiv.
1625: Sweden takes Livonia north of the Daugava.
July 1626: Sweden attacks Royal Prussia.
6 September 1629: the Truce of Altmark, 'valid for six years'.
1629: Sweden keeps Royal Prussian towns.

'The duchy existed until 1629, when most of its territory passed to the Swedish Empire'; 'their gains were recognized in the Truce of Altmark in 1629'; 'The Commonwealth retained southeastern parts of the Wenden Voivodeship', the Inflanty Voivodeship with its capital at Daugavpils.
Mirror of the duchy-of-livonia dissolve: the Commonwealth keeps the south-east as the Inflanty Voivodeship; The Deluge page names it: '(Latgale – the south-eastern part of Livonia)'.
October 1632: Muscovy attacks Smolensk.
June 1634: the Treaty of Polyanovka ends the Smolensk War.
June 1634: Serpeysk goes to Russia.
12 September 1635: the Treaty of Stuhmsdorf.
1637: 'After the childless death of the last Griffin duke, Bogislaw XIV in 1637, the land again became a terra of the Polish Crown'.
1644: 'Town of Trubchevsk' is listed as gained by Michael I of Russia from the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth.
25 January 1648: Khmelnytsky rises.
19 August 1649: the Treaty of Zboriv.
19 August 1649: Cossack autonomy under the crown.
1651: the war resumes; the page's dated clash is 28 June 1651 at Berestechko.
1651: the Treaty of Bila Tserkva.
1651: the autonomy shrinks.
1651: the Hetmanate's autonomy is confined to Kyiv Voivodeship (see the vassal_end). fx-37: counterpart repointed to cossack-hetmanate, as in ledger 35.
January 1654: the Hetmanate goes over to Russia.
January 1654: the Pereiaslav agreement takes the left bank out of the Commonwealth.
July 1654: Russia invades.
1654: Russia takes the north-east of the Grand Duchy.
23 September 1654: Smolensk falls.
December 1654: Russian troops 'swarmed over Polish Livonia' and 'established themselves at Ludza and Rezekne'.
1655: Russia takes the Lithuanian heartland.
July 1655: the Swedish invasion.
Nov-Dec 1655: 'the Swedish army under Gustaf Otto Stenbock captured all the towns of Royal Prussia except for Gdańsk, Puck and Malbork'.

6 November 1657: 'They signed the Treaty of Wehlau on 19 September 1657 and the Treaty of Bromberg on 6 November 1657'; 'achieved full sovereignty over the duchy under the 1657 Treaty of Wehlau' and John Casimir 'recognised Frederick William's full sovereignty over the Duchy of Prussia'.

1657: 'After the 1657 Treaty of Bydgoszcz (Bromberg)... it was granted as a fief to the Hohenzollern dynasty of Brandenburg-Prussia'; the Treaty of Bromberg was signed 'On November 6, 1657'. brandenburg-prussia /ledger/7 books the…
3 May 1660: the Treaty of Oliva ends the war with Sweden ('John II Casimir renounced his claim to the Swedish throne').

3 May 1660: 'the Treaty of Oliva was signed, which ended the Polish–Swedish War'; the page does not say when Swedish control of Royal Prussia ended (Toruń capitulated 30 December 1658; Grudziądz was taken 'In August 1659'; Brodnica surrendered soon after; 'In December 1659, the siege of Elbląg…
Bridging: the pages opened do not date the Commonwealth's recovery of the north-east of the Grand Duchy; Cliopatria's shape returns to the Commonwealth in 1662.
Bridging: as above; the Truce of Vilna (2 November, in the context of 1655) is the page's only Lithuanian truce and gives no recovery date.

The Truce of Andrusovo: 'ceded to Russia the fortress of Smolensk and Ukraine on the left bank of the Dnieper River (including Kiev)'; it 'kept right-bank Ukraine' (Russo-Polish War (1654–1667) page: 'January 1667').
January 1667: the Russian hold on Smolensk becomes a cession (see the loss).

Treaty of Oliva (1660) section of The Deluge page: Poland kept 'only part' of Livonia, '(Latgale – the south-eastern part of Livonia)', which 'was in Russian hands at the time, until the Armistice of Andrusov in 1667'.
January 1667: Andrusovo ends the thirteen-year war with Russia.
August 1672: the Ottoman invasion.
October 1672: the Peace of Buczacz.
1676: the Treaty of Żurawno.
1676: Żurawno ends the 1672-1676 war.
26 January 1699: the Treaty of Karlowitz.
1704: Charles XII sets up a rival king.
October 1706: Augustus II gives up the throne at Altranstädt.
October 1706: Altranstädt ends the contest for the throne (Augustus loses it).
1709: Augustus returns.
5 August 1772: the First Partition, Russia's share.
1772: the First Partition, Austria's share (see the Russian loss for the dates).
1772: the First Partition, Prussia's share (see the Russian loss for the dates).
1792: the Russian invasion.
23 January 1793: the occupation becomes annexation by the partition treaty ('signed during the Grodno Sejm on 23 January 1793 (without Austria)').
23 January 1793: the Second Partition, Russia's share: 250,200 km2 (34.11%).
23 January 1793: the Second Partition, Prussia's share: 57,100 km2 (7.78%), 'South Prussia, with Poznań as its capital'.
1794: the Kościuszko Uprising.
24 October 1795: the uprising's last act, the Third Partition treaty.

'With the signing of the final document on 24 October 1795, the Duchy of Courland was incorporated into the Russian Empire'; 'Duke Peter von Biron gave up his rights to Russia in 1795'; infobox: 'Third Partition of Poland: 28 March 1795'.
24 October 1795: the Third Partition, Russia's share: 120,000 km2 (16.36%) and 1.2 million people, 'including Vilnius'.
24 October 1795: Austria: 47,000 km2 (6.41%) and 1.2 million people, 'including Lublin and Kraków'.
24 October 1795: Prussia: 48,000 km2 (6.54%) in the table, 55,000 km2 and 1 million people 'including Warsaw' in the text.
24 October 1795: the Commonwealth is partitioned for the last time.

wars.name: Livonian War
wars.outcome: Báthory retakes Polotsk (30 August 1579) and campaigns to Velikie Luki (5 September 1580) and Pskov (1581); the Truce of Jam Zapolski (1582) gives the Commonwealth Livonia and Dorpat and leaves it Polotsk.

wars.name: Nalyvaiko Uprising
wars.outcome: Polish-Lithuanian victory: the Cossack tabor surrenders at Lubny (May-July 1596) and Nalyvaiko is executed.

wars.name: Polish–Russian War (1609–1618)
wars.outcome: The Truce of Deulino (11 December 1618, effective 4 January 1619) gives the Commonwealth the Smolensk and Chernihiv voivodeships: 'the largest geographical expansion of the Commonwealth (0.99 million km2)'.

wars.name: Polish–Swedish War (1621–1625)
wars.outcome: Sweden compels the cession of Livonia north of the Daugava in 1625; the Truce of Altmark (1629) confirms the loss of Riga.

wars.name: Polish–Swedish War (1626–1629)
wars.outcome: Truce of Altmark, 6 September 1629, valid six years: the Commonwealth 'acknowledges Swedish occupation of Livonia'; Sweden keeps Braunsberg, Frauenberg and Elbing in Royal Prussia and Pillau, Fischhausen, Lochstädt and Memel in East Prussia until the Treaty…

wars.name: Smolensk War
wars.outcome: Treaty of Polyanovka, June 1634: Russia accepts Polish-Lithuanian control of the Smolensk region, receives Serpeysk, pays 20,000 gold rubles; Władysław IV drops his claim to the Russian throne.

wars.name: Khmelnytsky Uprising
wars.outcome: Zboriv (19 August 1649) gives the Hetmanate autonomy in Kyiv, Bratslav and Chernihiv; Bila Tserkva (1651) confines it to Kyiv Voivodeship; Pereiaslav (January 1654) takes the Hetmanate to Russia; the infobox gives 'Emergence of the Cossack Hetmanate'.

wars.name: Russo-Polish War (1654–1667)
wars.outcome: Russia takes Smolensk (23 September 1654), Polotsk, Vitebsk, Minsk, Vilnius, Kaunas, Hrodno (1654-1655) and Ludza and Rezekne (December 1654); Andrusovo (January 1667) cedes Smolensk and left-bank Ukraine with Kyiv, and the Commonwealth keeps right-bank…

wars.name: The Deluge (history)
wars.outcome: Treaty of Oliva, 3 May 1660: Poland 'gave up most of Livonia, including Riga, and kept only Latgale'; John II Casimir renounces the Swedish throne; Ducal Prussia sovereign by Labiau (20 November 1656), Wehlau and Bromberg (6 November 1657).

wars.name: Polish–Ottoman War (1672–1676)
wars.outcome: Peace of Buczacz (October 1672) cedes Podole, Bracław and part of Kiev voivodeship and a tribute of 22,000 ducats; the Sejm does not ratify; Khotyn (11 November 1673) is a victory; Żurawno (1676) ends the tribute and returns Bila Tserkva and Pavoloch, the…

wars.name: Great Turkish War
wars.outcome: Treaty of Karlowitz, 26 January 1699: the Commonwealth recovers Podolia and gives back captured Moldavian fortresses.

wars.name: Great Northern War
wars.outcome: Charles XII invades Poland-Lithuania (1702), a Warsaw Confederation elects Leszczyński (1704, crowned 1705); Altranstädt (October 1706) dethrones Augustus II; after Poltava (1709) Augustus 'regained the Polish throne'; Nystad (1721) is between Russia and…

wars.name: Russo-Polish War of 1792
wars.outcome: Russian forces invade; the Targowica magnates fight the pro-constitution forces ('War in Defense of the Constitution'); the Second Partition (23 January 1793) annexes 307,300 km2.

wars.name: Kościuszko Uprising
wars.outcome: The uprising 'began' in 1794; the Third Partition treaty (24 October 1795) divides the remaining 215,000 km2 and Stanisław August abdicates (25 November 1795).

certainty.note: The eastern and southern frontiers (Muscovy, the Wild Fields, Moldavia, the Crimean khanate) are approximate; sharp lines only at the Truce of Jam Zapolski (1582) for Livonia and Polotsk, the Truce of Deulino (1619), the Truce of Altmark…

Fixed by treaty: Andrusovo (1667) with Russia, Buchach/Żurawno (1672/1676) and Karlowitz (1699) with the Ottomans, Oliva (1660) with Sweden and Brandenburg-Prussia; the south-eastern steppe edge (Zaporozhia, Podolian borderland) stays soft.
The partitions of 1772, 1793 and 1795 draw treaty lines with area figures; the Ottoman frontier on the Dniester is as before.
